title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page settles a lemma on divided powers for a principal ideal (π) in a p-adic ring V, presumably a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p). This is the setting of the crystalline / de Rham notes in this folder. Two questions are asked: (1) when is v_p(π^n/n!) ≥ 0 for all n, i.e. when does the ideal πV carry divided powers γ_n(x) = x^n/n!; (2) when does v_p(π^n/n!) → +∞, i.e. when are these divided powers topologically nilpotent (equivalently, when does exp converge on πV).

Step 1 is Legendre's formula. Write s_p(n) = 'chif(n)' for the sum of the base-p digits of n. Then v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p−1), so (p−1)·v_p(π^n/n!) = n[(p−1)v_p(π) − 1] + s_p(n).

Step 2 gives the divided-power criterion. Non-negativity for every n is equivalent to (p−1)v_p(π) ≥ 1 − s_p(n)/n for every n. Grothendieck shows s_p(n)/n → 0: if n = a_0 + … + a_ν p^ν with a_ν ≠ 0, then s_p(n) ≤ (p−1)(ν+1) and n ≥ p^ν. The supremum of the right-hand side is therefore 1 (approached along n = p^k, where s_p = 1). Hence π^n/n! ∈ V for all n ⟺ v_p(π) ≥ 1/(p−1) ⟺ π^{p−1} ∈ pV. In that case v_p(π^n/n!) ≥ s_p(n)/(p−1) > 0 for all n ≥ 1, so '≥0 for all n' upgrades to '>0 for all n'.

Step 3 gives the convergence criterion. If v_p(π) = 1/(p−1), the valuation equals s_p(n)/(p−1), which does not tend to infinity (it equals 1/(p−1) at n = p^k). If v_p(π) > 1/(p−1), it equals (αn + s_p(n))/(p−1) with α > 0, which grows like αn/(p−1) → ∞. So topological nilpotence ⟺ v_p(π) > 1/(p−1). For π a uniformizer this reads p = unit·π^r with r = e < p−1.

These are the familiar conditions: e ≤ p−1 for the maximal ideal of a DVR to have (unique) divided powers, and e < p−1 for them to be topologically nilpotent / for exp to converge. The 'pag. 30' marginal note suggests the lemma serves a step on p. 30 of the main manuscript.
errors: The line 'chif(n) ≤ 1' is evidently a slip or abbreviation for chif(n)/n ≤ 1 (the deleted line above it says chif(n)/n is 'tjrs ≤ 1'); taken literally it is false.
In the final estimate Grothendieck writes chif(n)/n ≤ (p−1)ν/p^ν. From his own bound chif(n) ≤ (p−1)(ν+1) one gets (p−1)(ν+1)/p^ν. This is harmless, since both tend to 0.
The deleted claim that chif(n)/n is a decreasing function of n is false (e.g. p=2: chif(2)/2 = 1/2 < chif(3)/3 = 2/3). Grothendieck rightly struck it out.
The final reformulation 'p = unit·π^r with r < p−1' presupposes π is a uniformizer, or at least that v(p)/v(π) is an integer. In general the condition is just v_p(π) > 1/(p−1).
The large brackets [ ] around (n − chif(n))/(p−1) are just grouping, not integer part; Legendre's formula is exact, so nothing is lost.

ideas.what: Legendre's formula v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p−1) via base-p digit sum
Ideal πV of a p-adic DVR has divided powers iff v_p(π) ≥ 1/(p−1), i.e. ramification e ≤ p−1
ideas.modern_name: Canonical PD-structure on the maximal ideal of a DVR with e ≤ p−1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in crystalline cohomology: Grothendieck's 1966 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés), Berthelot's thesis (1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates–Jussila, Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968), where the e ≤ p−1 condition for divided powers is discussed

ideas.what: π^n/n! → 0 iff v_p(π) > 1/(p−1), i.e. e < p−1 (topologically nilpotent divided powers / convergence of exp)
ideas.modern_name: Radius of convergence of the p-adic exponential; topologically PD-nilpotent ideal
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical p-adic analysis; e < p−1 later central in Raynaud's 1974 work on finite flat group schemes and in Fontaine–Laffaille

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary verification of the standard e ≤ p−1 / e < p−1 criteria for divided powers and their topological nilpotence, via Legendre's formula. It is classical and well known in the crystalline literature; the page is of interest only as a working computation behind Grothendieck's crystals notes.

Struck line reads roughly 'chif(n)/n fonction décroissante de n, tjrs ≤ 1' — the whole line is crossed out, consistent with the transcription.
In the line 'si v_p(π) > 1/(p−1), on a ... αn + chif(n)', the inserted '{+α > 0,+}' is written above the expression, and the expression is followed by ', qui tend vers +∞'.
